samples.summary: The v1 REST contract changes (new 409 on `POST .../move` for a merge straddling the freeze, new 409 on `PUT .../merges`, `PUT .../freeze` now answering with a *snapped* boundary that may exceed the requested one, and new 400s from the merge-count / covered-cell caps in `parseMerges`) are recorded only in `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md`. `docs/design/rest-api.md` is the canonical doc for this surface — §5.4 still says the single merge-related refusal is "A move that would split a merged range returns 409" — and is not touched by the diff, so the REST doc now understates the endpoints' behaviour.

`YorkieStore.applyMerge` makes the CRDT store silently drop a merge write that exceeds the budget, which (a) puts a business invariant in the persistence layer that no other `Store` implementation enforces (`MemStore.setMerge` and `readonly.ts` do not), so engine behaviour now depends on which store is plugged in, and (b) leaves `Sheet.merges` holding a block the store refused, diverging until reload. `docs/design/frontend.md`'s YorkieStore table (`setMerge(anchor, span)` → "Write to root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref]") is not updated for the new conditional behaviour.

`parseMerges` keeps its own per-span `rs * cs > MaxMergedCells` check and error message alongside the shared `mergeBudgetError`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` predicate the same commit introduces precisely so every writer spends one budget. The constant is imported so the value cannot drift, but the rule is now expressed in two places (engine predicate and backend loop) with two different messages.

The change bundles at least five separable concerns: merge propagation through copy/cut/paste, the merge-vs-freeze invariant across paste/drag-move/reorder/shift/three REST endpoints, a brand-new resource-limit regime (MaxMergeEntries / MaxMergeCoveredCells) threaded through five writers, a copy-buffer lifetime redesign (paste no longer clears the buffer, plus axis-ID revalidation on remote reload), and an unrelated `rangeOf` spread-argument fix. No originating issue was supplied to scope this against, and each of the last three could ship independently; the breadth makes the change hard to accept or revert piecewise.

The XLSX importer now silently skips `mergeCell` entries once the budget is exhausted, a fidelity loss on import with no reporting channel (the file has no warn/notice mechanism). Consistent with its other `continue`s, but `docs/design/sheets/file-import.md` records nothing about merge import or its new ceiling.
